title: A Twist of Fate: The Helix-Turn-Helix Motif in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ExsA Can Allosterically Stabilize the Ligand-Binding Domain.
authors: Medarametla, Prasanthi; Greenhalgh, Jack Calum; Pohner, Ina; Welch, Martin; Poso, Antti; Kronenberger, Thales; Rahman, Taufiq
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过原子级MD模拟研究转录因子ExsA全长蛋白与DNA结合的构象动态及互作界面，并预测可成药口袋，聚焦TF-DNA结合机制，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic human pathogen. One of the most potent virulence factors in its arsenal is the type III secretion system (T3SS). This secretion apparatus injects effector toxins directly into host cells, thereby causing cytotoxicity. The expression of all components of T3SS is regulated by a master transcriptional regulator, ExsA. The inhibition of the latter should therefore lead to the suppression of P. aeruginosa virulence. However, to date, no drugs targeting ExsA have reached the market, and only static structural models of the protein have been generated, focusing on the C-terminal domain (CTD). Here, we used mus atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the conformational dynamics of full-length ExsA bound to DNA or DNA free, investigated as monomers or dimers. Our data show how the CTD and NTD of ExsA likely interact with one another and how ExsA binds to DNA. We also analyzed the MD trajectories to predict potential druggable pocket(s) in the structure and relevant geometry. This revealed a lipid-binding pocket within the beta-sheet bundle and identified two novel potentially druggable pockets at the NTD/CTD interface, which could be used in future structure-based drug discovery campaigns. Overall, a single helix-turn-helix motif seems to drive DNA recognition in each ExsA monomer and to stabilize the putative ligand-binding domain.
abstract_zh: 铜绿假单胞菌是一种机会性人类病原体。其毒力因子中最强效之一是三型分泌系统（T3SS）。该分泌装置将效应毒素直接注入宿主细胞，从而引起细胞毒性。T3SS所有组分的表达受主转录调控因子ExsA的调控。因此，抑制后者应能导致铜绿假单胞菌毒力被抑制。然而，迄今为止，尚无靶向ExsA的药物上市，且仅生成了蛋白质的静态结构模型，重点关注C端结构域（CTD）。在此，我们使用mus原子级分子动力学（MD）模拟来研究全长ExsA与DNA结合或未结合DNA时的构象动态，并以单体或二聚体形式进行研究。我们的数据展示了ExsA的CTD和NTD可能如何相互作用，以及ExsA如何与DNA结合。我们还分析了MD轨迹，以预测结构中潜在的可成药口袋及其相关几何形状。这揭示了β-折叠束内的一个脂质结合口袋，并识别出NTD/CTD界面处的两个新型潜在可成药口袋，这些可用于未来的基于结构的药物发现活动。总体而言，单个螺旋-转角-螺旋基序似乎驱动每个ExsA单体中的DNA识别，并稳定推定配体结合结构域。
